findings.consequence: No temperature extremes can be read from NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 at this version.
findings.documented: docs/sources/cmip6.md:5 says NEX uses the four recipes txx, tnn, rx1day and rx5day; line 36 says temperatures must be kelvin.
evidence: docs/reports/u1-nex-bytes-fix.md (crc-lab): real file headers, failing test, fix
check records nex-gddp-cmip6/units[txx ...] and units[tnn ...] (site/validation/data/records/nex-gddp-cmip6.json), run of 2026-11-12
findings.observed: The files declare kelvin, but h5netcdf returns the one-character unit as bytes (b'K') and the unit check compares its text form with 'K'. The call raises: 'tasmax' is published in "b'K'", but recipe 'txx' converts from 'K'. Precipitation is unaffected.
findings.title: Temperature recipes (txx, tnn) fail on real NEX files

findings.consequence: A gridded curve can rest on far fewer years than the request suggests where data are missing; the number of years behind each cell's fit should be checked before use.
findings.documented: docs/sources/jrc.md:58: 'The curated policy fits the lower tail and requires at least 20 complete years.' The policy's own error message says it 'requires at least 20 complete years' (crc_sdk/workflows/blocks.py:126-129).
findings.observed: validate_years compares the number of years in the request with minimum_years (crc_sdk/workflows/blocks.py:124-125). Each grid cell is then fitted when it has at least 4 valid annual values (MINIMUM_BLOCKS = 4, crc_sdk/connectors/blocks.py:60; minimum_blocks=4 in crc_sdk/providers/era5.py:566 and crc_sdk/providers/cmip6.py:1052). Station sources apply minimum_years per station.
findings.title: The 20-year minimum counts the years requested, not the years valid in each cell

findings.consequence: A JRC flood or EDO file, once moved away from its cache, does not say under which licence or from which bytes it was made.
findings.documented: docs/data-licences.md:14-15: 'Every canonical file records source.licence, source.attribution, retrieved_at and checksum (schema 1.3), so outputs self-describe.'
evidence: check records jrc-flood/provenance[*] (draft records data/cache/validation/drafts/records/jrc-flood.json), run of 2026-11-17
findings.observed: Those fields are written only when the curve source supplies a CurveSourceInfo (crc_sdk/connectors/adapters.py:309). The JRC and EDO modules define none; the JRC workflow only rewrites the uri (crc_sdk/workflows/jrc.py:521-534). Checksums of the cropped inputs are kept in the cache manifest, not in the output file. Shown on five real JRC flood outputs on 2026-11-17 (GloFAS for the Texas box, Houston, Austin and Fremont; EFAS for the Rhine box): in each, licence, attribution, retrieved_at and checksum are empty. Not yet shown for jrc-edo, where it is still code reading.
findings.title: JRC flood and EDO output files do not carry licence, attribution, retrieval time or checksum

findings.consequence: An EDO file and an ERA5 or CMIP6 file built over the same years would carry different horizons and would not join on the row key.
findings.documented: docs/design-decisions.md:28-30: for a window, 'horizon = centre year (start + end) // 2'. docs/sources/cmip6.md:42: 'horizon is the window centre'.
findings.observed: The EDO provider sets the year of its record to max(years) (crc_sdk/providers/jrc_edo.py:217).
findings.title: EDO drought curves are labelled with the last year of the record, not the centre year

findings.consequence: A year with most of its record missing still contributes an annual minimum to the fit.
findings.documented: crc_sdk/connectors/blocks.py:20-30 states the convention for block statistics: a block needs a minimum fraction of valid days.
findings.observed: The EDO annual value is np.nanmin over whatever ten-day values exist in the year (crc_sdk/providers/jrc_edo.py:255), so one valid value makes a year.
findings.title: The EDO annual minimum has no completeness rule

findings.consequence: If a store changed its units, ERA5 values would be converted wrongly without an error.
findings.observed: The CMIP6 and NEX readers refuse a variable whose units attribute differs from the recipe's (crc_sdk/providers/cmip6.py:946-958). The ERA5 provider reads a units attribute only for the time axis (crc_sdk/providers/era5.py:244) and applies the kelvin and metre conversions unconditionally.
findings.title: ERA5 values are converted without checking the unit the store declares

findings.consequence: The field cannot be used to tell when the release was actually fetched.
findings.documented: docs/data-licences.md:20-21: 'the retrieval date and checksum are the audit trail.'
findings.observed: When a selection is materialised, retrieved_at is set to the current time (crc_sdk/workflows/crc_open.py:600), also when the partitions come from a warm cache.
findings.title: retrieved_at in a CRC Open file is the time the file was written, not the time the data were downloaded

findings.consequence: An OS-Climate output file may carry no licence.
findings.documented: docs/data-licences.md:38: 'OS-Climate layers | Read from layer metadata | Per layer'.
findings.observed: A search of crc_sdk/providers/os_climate.py for licence handling finds none. Only that file was searched.
findings.title: The OS-Climate licence is documented as read from layer metadata; no code that reads it was found

findings.consequence: Two runs of the same request can return different data with nothing in the output to show it.
findings.documented: docs/development.md:25-26: 'Every adapter records licence, attribution, retrieval time and checksums in canonical metadata or its cache manifest.'
findings.observed: The request defaults to branch 'main' of the Source Cooperative repository, not a fixed snapshot (crc_sdk/connectors/agriculture.py:100). Rows carry a source path only.
findings.title: The Cropland Data Layer is read from a moving branch and its output records no provenance

findings.consequence: Currently active storms cannot be read through IBTrACSPlan at this version. The other subsets are unaffected.
findings.documented: crc_sdk/workflows/ibtracs.py:28-41 lists "active" among the eleven accepted subsets; the error message for any other spelling names it as valid. docs/sources/observations.md:29 documents basin subsets only.
findings.observed: crc-sdk requests .../ibtracs.active.list.v04r01.csv and NOAA answers 404. NOAA's directory holds ibtracs.ACTIVE.list.v04r01.csv (capitals). IBTrACSPlan("active", ...).prefetch() raises HTTPError 404; IBTrACSPlan("ACTIVE", ...) is refused as an invalid subset. The other ten names are served.
findings.title: The subset "active" is accepted but NOAA has no file under that name

findings.consequence: A user who passes the batches on must copy the citation and terms from the manifest or from prefetch(); nothing in the data carries them.
findings.documented: AGENTS.md (crc-sdk) asks contributors to 'record licence, attribution, retrieval time and checksums for every source'. docs/data-licences.md:36 lists IBTrACS as a U.S. government work with attribution requested.
findings.observed: The manifest written beside the snapshot holds url, version, subset, sha256, retrieved_at, etag, last_modified, units, terms_url and citation (crc_sdk/workflows/ibtracs.py:139-153). It has no licence field. The Arrow batches returned by batches() have no schema metadata, so the provenance travels only in the cache directory.
findings.title: The snapshot's manifest has a terms address and a citation but no licence field; the batches carry no provenance

findings.consequence: A user cannot read NASA's latest revision through crc-sdk, and the default (1.0) is the oldest. The differences seen here are small; other models, variables and regions were not compared. NASA's technical note for version 2.0 (31 May 2025, section 4.3) states that tasmax and tasmin were reprocessed in their entirety with a corrected observational reference (an artifact over central Canada) and that values were swapped in grid cells where the maximum was below the minimum; that anomalously large pr values in cells with an extremely small daily climatology were adjusted; and that bounds were applied to hurs, huss, rlds and sfcWind. These corrections are in version 2.0 only.
findings.documented: docs/sources/cmip6.md:73: 'File revisions 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 are selected explicitly'. crc_sdk/workflows/nex.py:84-85 refuses any other version.
evidence: NASA technical note for version 2.0, sections 3.2.2.1 and 4.3 (docs/validation/references/nex-gddp-cmip6-v2/README.md)
findings.observed: For ACCESS-CM2 r1i1p1f1, NASA's archive holds files ending in _v2.0.nc for tasmax, tasmin and pr, in both years checked (historical 2014, ssp585 2050). They were uploaded on 1 July 2025 and carry the attribute version = '2.0'. No version 1.2 file exists for these; version 1.1 exists for pr only. In the Texas box the annual one-day rainfall from 2.0 equals that from 1.1 and differs from 1.0 in 15 of 2,158 cells in 2014 (by at most 0.08 mm) and 42 cells in 2050 (by at most 0.84 mm); the annual maximum temperature from 2.0 equals that from 1.0.
findings.title: NASA serves files of version 2.0, which cannot be requested

findings.consequence: A small share of pixels (about 3 in 10,000 here) that have depths at four or more return periods get no curve although one exists, and nothing in the output says so. Whether a pixel is fitted depends on the last digits of its depths.
findings.documented: docs/sources/jrc.md:33-39 says the plan 'caches AOI crops, then fits'; no page says that a fit can fail. crc_sdk/connectors/adapters.py:432-433 raises 'quantile optimizer did not converge' when crc-framework's fit_quantiles reports no convergence, and the curated JRC policy sets on_fit_failure = 'skip' (crc_sdk/workflows/jrc.py:53).
evidence: check records jrc-flood/curves[glofas-tx], curves[glofas-houston], curves[glofas-fremont], curves[efas-rhine] (draft records data/cache/validation/drafts/records/jrc-flood.json), run of 2026-11-17
findings.observed: A least-squares line through the same points has an exact solution; the independent reference computes it for every such pixel. crc-framework 0.6.0 does not return one for 2,821 pixels of the Texas box, 82 of the Houston box, 5 of the Fremont box and 49 of the Rhine box (0 of the Austin box); the Houston and Austin boxes lie inside the Texas box. Each has several equal depths followed by larger ones, for example 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2.639, 3.768 m. Called directly, fit_quantiles(family='gumbel_r') on that series raises 'gumbel_r fitting did not converge after 374 iterations' when the depths are the 32-bit numbers of the file, and converges after 91 iterations when the same depths are given as decimal numbers. crc-sdk writes no row and no message for these pixels. For every pixel both sides fitted, location and scale agree within 1.2e-6 m (two of 19,702,276 parameters in the Texas box differ by more than the tolerance of 1e-6 m, the larger by 1.1e-6 m).
findings.title: The quantile fit gives up on depths that are flat and then rise, and crc-sdk then drops the pixel without a message

findings.consequence: A place the publisher's map floods only at long return periods (100 years and more), or at a constant 1 m, is absent from the output in the same way as a place that never floods. A user reading the output as 'no row means no flood' undercounts flooded area by the shares above. What the constant 1 m stands for in the publisher's data was not established.
findings.documented: docs/sources/jrc.md does not mention pixels left out. The rules are in the code: four or more finite depths (crc_sdk/connectors/adapters.py:658-663), a fit failure is skipped (adapters.py:702-716, crc_sdk/workflows/jrc.py:53), and the curated policy writes no diagnostics file (jrc.py:57-81).
evidence: check records jrc-flood/curves[*] and exploration tables 'Wet pixels that get no curve', 'Published wet pixels without a curve, by return period' (draft records data/cache/validation/drafts/records/jrc-flood.json), run of 2026-11-17
findings.observed: Share of the pixels that have a depth at some return period and get no curve: Texas box 1,832,251 of 11,686,210 (15.7%), Houston 65,705 of 278,654 (23.6%), Austin 3,293 of 25,494 (12.9%), Fremont 2,734 of 10,603 (25.8%), Rhine (EFAS) 18,824 of 161,898 (11.6%). By cause in the Texas box: fewer than four depths 941,251; all depths equal 698,317 (every one of them at exactly 1 m at every return period); a depth lower than at a shorter return period 192,683; the fit not converging 2,821 (CRC-013-FWK). At the 500-year return period 1,832,250 of the 11,686,209 flooded pixels of the Texas box have no curve; at 10 years 890,968 of 9,255,575. The reference applies the same rules and names the same pixels, apart from those of CRC-013-FWK.
findings.title: A pixel the publisher shows flooded gets no curve, and no message, when it has fewer than four depths, equal depths or a decreasing depth

findings.consequence: Evaluated at 10 to 50 years, the output shows water where the publisher's map has none and negative depths where it has water; the documentation says the values are not bit-for-bit but gives no size. A user who needs the published depth at a published return period cannot get it from the output. Distances computed by the reference from its own fit, which equals crc-sdk's within 1.2e-6 m.
findings.documented: docs/sources/jrc.md:38-39: 'Fitted values at source return periods are curve evaluations, not bit-for-bit source pixels.' The curated policy sets no limit on the misfit (crc_sdk/workflows/jrc.py:50-56; maximum_normalized_rmse and maximum_absolute_residual are None).
evidence: exploration tables 'How far the fitted curve lies from the published depths' and 'Curve where the publisher is dry, and curve below zero' (draft records data/cache/validation/drafts/records/jrc-flood.json), run of 2026-11-17
check records jrc-flood/values[*] (draft records data/cache/validation/drafts/records/jrc-flood.json), run of 2026-11-17
findings.observed: Largest distance between the curve and a published depth, per fitted pixel: Texas box median 0.039 m, 99th percentile 0.60 m, largest 26.4 m, above 1 m in 31,771 of 9,853,959 pixels; Houston median 0.040 m, largest 3.1 m; Austin median 0.095 m, largest 1.2 m; Fremont median 0.017 m, largest 2.0 m; Rhine median 0.092 m, largest 8.7 m, above 1 m in 654 of 143,074. At the 10-year return period, pixels with no published depth where the curve gives 0.1 m or more: Texas 493,550, Houston 14,678, Austin 782, Fremont 593, Rhine 5,709 (largest value at a dry return period: 53.9 m in the Texas box). Pixels whose curve is below zero at 10 years: Texas 604,768, Houston 21,124, Austin 2,075, Fremont 362, Rhine 15,293. At 100 years and longer neither occurs in any area.
findings.title: The fitted curve can be positive where the publisher's map is dry, below zero where it is wet, and metres away from the published depth

findings.consequence: The user learns that nothing intersects but not why; a caller that catches one error type misses the other.
findings.documented: docs/sources/jrc.md does not say what happens outside the coverage. EFAS's README gives its extent (longitude -24.54 to 67.26, latitude 27.81 to 71.13).
evidence: check records jrc-flood/coverage[efas-tx], coverage[efas-fremont] (draft records data/cache/validation/drafts/records/jrc-flood.json), run of 2026-11-17
findings.observed: HazardDataset.efas for the Texas box and for the Fremont box, with a cache: LookupError 'no JRC resources intersect area (-106.645646, 25.837377, -93.508292, 36.500704)' after 1.0 s and 0.7 s; nothing in the message names EFAS's extent or says that the box is outside it. Read in the code, not run: without a cache (stream mode) the same request raises ValueError 'bounds do not intersect the raster' (crc_sdk/connectors/duckdb/geotiff.py:289-292).
findings.title: A request outside a dataset's coverage ends with an error that does not name the coverage, and the error differs with the cache mode

findings.consequence: If the publisher replaces a depth file without changing the README line, two runs with the same pinned version read different bytes and nothing records it. The crops in a cache can be checked against the manifest; the publisher's file cannot. No such replacement was observed.
findings.documented: docs/sources/jrc.md:33-34: 'materialize() resolves latest once and pins the version in the cache manifest and canonical provenance'.
evidence: check records jrc-flood/files[glofas], files[efas], manifest[*] and exploration table 'The publisher's releases' (draft records data/cache/validation/drafts/records/jrc-flood.json), run of 2026-11-17
findings.observed: The version is the text after 'Dataset version' in README.txt (crc_sdk/providers/jrc.py:155-176); the depth files are at addresses without a version (.../flood_hazard/RP100/ID38_N30_W100_RP100_depth.tif). The cache manifest holds the SHA-256 of each local crop, not of the publisher's file. On 2026-11-17 the publisher's directory showed, for GloFAS: README 'Dataset version 2.1.2', README last updated 12.01.2026 and modified 2026-10-21, depth files dated 2025-12-17 to 2025-12-18, return-period folders modified 2026-10-30; for EFAS: version 3.1.1, depth files dated 2026-03-03 to 2026-03-05. Read in the code, not run: a later run that finds a manifest does not ask the publisher again (crc_sdk/workflows/jrc.py:362-365).
findings.title: The release is identified by one line of the publisher's README; the file addresses hold no version and no publisher checksum is taken

findings.consequence: Which licence governs is the publisher's to say; the Open Database License has a share-alike condition that CC BY 4.0 does not. A user relying on crc-sdk's statement has not been told that the publisher's README says otherwise.
findings.documented: docs/sources/jrc.md:5-6: 'Both sources are CC BY 4.0; cite JRC and the product version.' docs/data-licences.md:31: 'JRC EFAS / GloFAS flood | CC-BY-4.0'.
evidence: publisher files README.txt and copyright.txt of CEMS-GLOFAS/flood_hazard and CEMS-EFAS/flood_hazard, read 2026-11-17 (checksums in the draft records)
check records jrc-flood/provenance[*] and exploration table 'The publisher's releases' (draft records data/cache/validation/drafts/records/jrc-flood.json), run of 2026-11-17
findings.observed: README.txt of both datasets, line A02: 'License information, restrictions on use: Open Data Commons Open Database License v1.0'. copyright.txt in the same directories: 'Any copyright and/or sui generis right on the dataset is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) licence'. The two publisher files name different licences; crc-sdk's documentation agrees with copyright.txt. The licence is written in crc-sdk's documentation only: it is not read from the publisher and not written into the output (CRC-003-JRC).
findings.title: crc-sdk states CC BY 4.0 for the JRC flood maps; the publisher's README names the Open Database License

findings.consequence: Depths the publisher itself marks as doubtful reach the user unmarked; in the Fremont box every depth above 10 m is of that kind. Depths above 10 m outside the mask (most of those in the Texas box) are not explained by it; whether they are permanent water bodies was not examined.
findings.documented: docs/sources/jrc.md does not mention them. GloFAS README (F01 and the file description): the release includes, per tile, 'the permanent water bodies used to patch the flood hazard maps' and 'the spurious depth map that identifies areas where depths >10m are predicted in small channels (<3,000km^2) for the 10-year return period, plus a 2km buffer'. EFAS holds Europe_permanent_water_bodies.tif and Europe_spurious_depth_areas.tif.
evidence: publisher file README.txt of CEMS-GLOFAS/flood_hazard, lines 38-49, read 2026-11-17
exploration table 'Depths above 10 m and the publisher's spurious-depth mask' (draft records data/cache/validation/drafts/records/jrc-flood.json), run of 2026-11-17
findings.observed: crc-sdk requests the depth files only (crc_sdk/providers/jrc.py:186-246). In the GloFAS tiles read here, pixels inside the spurious-depth mask: Texas box 268,433, Austin 1,245, Fremont 5,137, Houston 0. Pixels deeper than 10 m at 100 years, and how many of them lie inside the mask: Fremont 126, all 126 inside; Austin 2,201, 21 inside; Texas box 192,437, 8,393 inside. Largest depth: Texas box 108.2 m, Austin 21.8 m, Fremont 20.5 m, Houston 10.1 m, Rhine 22.9 m. These depths are fitted and delivered like any other. The EFAS mask and both permanent-water layers were not read by the assessment.
findings.title: The publisher's masks of spurious depths and permanent water are not read

findings.consequence: Outputs for two boxes cannot be joined, compared or de-duplicated on source_id, and the same request with and without a cache gives different ids for the same pixel.
findings.documented: docs/concepts.md:43 gives the row key as (hazard_name, horizon, pathway, cell_index, source_id). No page says what source_id is made from.
evidence: check records jrc-flood/source-id[*] (draft records data/cache/validation/drafts/records/jrc-flood.json), run of 2026-11-17
findings.observed: source_id is the SHA-256 of the dataset name, the tile and the pixel's row and column (crc_sdk/connectors/adapters.py:299-301, 741-743); with a cache the row and column are those of the local crop (crc_sdk/workflows/jrc.py:502-511). All 22,201 fitted pixels of the Austin box are also in the Texas-box output with the same curve (difference of location 0); of 2,000 of them compared, 0 have the same source_id in the two outputs. Per area, the ids equal the reference's computed from the crop position in every sampled pixel, and equal the position in the publisher's file in 0 of 2,000 (621 of 2,000 in the Texas box, where the crops of two tiles begin at the tile's first row and column). Without a cache the position is the file's (read in the code, not run).
findings.title: With a cache, a pixel's source_id depends on the box asked for

findings.consequence: A cache built with a relative path (as in the documentation's example, .cache('cache/efas', mode='reuse')) stops working offline when it is moved, mounted elsewhere or used by a job started in another folder. The message says the resources are missing or invalid, though the files are present and unchanged.
findings.documented: No page says a cache is tied to the working folder it was made from. The documentation's example uses a relative path (docs/sources/jrc.md:19).
findings.observed: The manifest stores each crop's path as the cache path was given (for .cache('cache', ...): 'cache/aoi/rp10-....tif'). A run in offline mode from another working folder, given the absolute path of the same cache, ends with FileNotFoundError 'cems-glofas-river-flood cannot be materialized offline; missing or invalid cached AOI resources: ID18_N40_W130:RP10, ...'; from the working folder the cache was made in, the same run completes. Tried on the Fremont box with four return periods.
findings.title: A cache made under a relative path cannot be read offline from another working folder

findings.consequence: A user asking for a state or a country should expect tens of minutes and several GB per run, with nothing kept if the run stops before the end; a larger box may not fit in memory. One machine, one run.
findings.documented: docs/sources/jrc.md gives no time or size. Its example is a box of 0.7 by 0.5 degrees.
evidence: exploration table 'crc-sdk's runs' (draft records data/cache/validation/drafts/records/jrc-flood.json), run of 2026-11-17
findings.observed: GloFAS for the Texas box (201,757,502 pixels in four tiles, 9,851,138 curves, 10,703,386 rows): 1,604 s and a peak of 5,804 MB on an arm64 Mac with 16 GB, the 28 crops (about 0.6 GB at the publisher) fetched in the same run. The smaller boxes took 10 s (Austin, 22,201 curves) to 54 s (Houston, 212,867 curves). The table is validated in a separate worker process (crc_sdk/connectors/parquet.py:232), which fails with BrokenProcessPool when the calling script is read from standard input. Read in the code: the output file is written only at the end of the run.
findings.title: A state-sized box is fitted pixel by pixel in one process: 27 minutes and 5.8 GB of memory for the Texas box

sources.notes: The inputs behind the release are not public, so a comparison with an original (tier 2) is limited to the release's own catalogue and checksums. Assessed mainly by validation (tier 3).
sources.purpose: Ready-made hazard curves on H3 cells for 63 hazards under SSP5-8.5, for screening asset portfolios.
sources.tier_reason: Tier 1: feeds a crc-lab result today, or is the release most CRC users consume. Feeds the eight CRC Open hazard layers of the Texas data explorer.
sources.title: CRC Open hosted release

sources.notes: Draft. Assessed on the 1.5 degree store (wb2-1p5), the Texas box (80 grid cells), the rainfall recipes for 2021, with and without the land mask. One variable-year of this store is about 0.9 GB whatever the box, because every chunk covers the globe. The temperature recipes, the 0.25 degree store and the fitted curves were not run.
sources.publisher: ECMWF / Copernicus C3S (public Zarr copies by Google and WeatherBench2)
sources.purpose: A historical baseline of annual temperature and rainfall extremes on H3 cells, comparable with the projection recipes.

statement.note: Confirmed for wb2-1p5 only. arco-0p25 was not opened: one variable-year there is about 8,800 global chunks.
statement.text: Opens one of two public Zarr copies of hourly ERA5 anonymously, with zarr over gcsfs: `arco-0p25` (the default, gs://gcp-public-data-arco-era5/ar/full_37-1h-0p25deg-chunk-1.zarr-v3, 0.25 degree) or `wb2-1p5` (gs://weatherbench2/datasets/era5/1959-2022-1h-240x121_equiangular_with_poles_conservative.zarr, 1.5 degree). No checksum of the hourly data is taken.

Names the release `final-through-<date>`. The date is the store's `valid_time_stop` attribute; for a store without it (wb2-1p5) it is 31 December of a year written in the code, 2022. Only `latest` or that name is accepted.

Accepts the years from the store's first year (1959 for wb2-1p5, written in the code) to the last complete year of that release; for rainfall the last year must be followed by one more day of record. The years are not compared with the store's time axis: hours the axis does not hold are skipped without an error.
Decodes the time axis from its `units` attribute (`hours`, `days` or `seconds since <date>`) as whole numbers; the `calendar` attribute is not read. Days are UTC days.
Reads `2m_temperature` for `txx` and `tnn` and `total_precipitation` for `rx1day` and `rx5day`, and requires the array to have exactly the dimensions time, latitude and longitude, in any order.

statement.note: The check confirms that the assumption holds for wb2-1p5 today. That the attribute is not read is shown in the offline tests on a constructed store that declares another unit (see finding CRC-006-ERA5).
statement.text: Assumes 2 m temperature in kelvin and precipitation in metres. The `units` attribute the store declares for the variable is not read.

statement.note: Confirmed for a box of 8 by 10 cells. A box narrower than one cell and a box at the 180 degree meridian were not run.
statement.text: Selects the grid cells whose centres lie inside the box grown by half a cell on every side, with longitudes brought to -180..180 and ordered west to east. A box narrower than one cell is widened to two cells. The same box is applied a second time to the stored annual file.
With `land_only`, keeps a cell only where the store's `land_sea_mask` is 0.5 or more; the others get no value.

statement.note: The chunks read from the publisher hold no NaN in the box. Missing hours inside a chunk were exercised in the offline tests only; absent chunks were exercised by the years the reference copy does not hold. The reading of an absent chunk as NaN is zarr's behaviour and has no line in crc-sdk.
statement.text: Treats a value that is not finite as missing. A chunk the store does not hold is read as the array's fill value (NaN), so it is missing too, without an error.

statement.note: Not run on the publisher's data in this draft (one variable-year is about 0.7 GB). Confirmed on constructed files only.
statement.text: Subtracts 273.15 from every hourly temperature, before any reduction, to give degrees Celsius.
Multiplies every hourly precipitation value by 1,000, before any reduction, to give millimetres.

statement.note: Not run on the publisher's data in this draft. Confirmed on constructed files only.
statement.text: The daily maximum (`txx`) or minimum (`tnn`) is taken over the hours stamped 00:00 to 23:00 UTC; a day needs at least 18 of its 24 hours.
An hourly precipitation value is counted in the UTC day of its stamp less one hour (the value stamped 00:00 belongs to the day before). A day is the sum of its 24 hours and needs all 24.

statement.note: In the year read every cell has 364 of 365 days, so the 90 per cent line itself was crossed only in the offline tests.
statement.text: Gives a grid cell an annual value only when at least 90 per cent of the year's days have a value (329 of 365, 330 of 366).

statement.note: Not run on the publisher's data in this draft. Confirmed on constructed files only.
statement.text: `txx` is the highest daily maximum of the year and `tnn` the lowest daily minimum.

`rx1day` is the largest daily total of the year. `rx5day` is the largest sum over five consecutive days that all have a value and lie within the year; windows do not reach into the neighbouring years.

statement.note: The 32-bit rounding is confirmed by the annual values. The manifest and the reuse of stored years were not exercised: every run used an empty cache folder.
statement.text: Keeps each year's values for the recipe and area as 32-bit floats in one small NetCDF file, listed with its checksum in a manifest; the annual values returned are those 32-bit values. Hourly data is never kept. The file's name does not depend on the release.

`annual_extremes()` returns one row per year and grid cell that has a value: year, latitude and longitude of the cell centre as the store writes them (longitude in -180..180), value in the recipe's unit; ordered by year, then in the store's latitude order, then west to east.

statement.note: Not checked: the fitting belongs to a later tier. A request of four years was accepted and one of fewer was not tried (finding CRC-002-FWK is about this rule).
statement.text: Refuses a request of fewer years than `minimum_years` (20 by default, never fewer than 4). Each grid cell is then fitted when it has at least 4 annual values.

statement.note: Not checked: the fitted curve (family, method, assignment to H3 cells) belongs to a later tier.
statement.text: Fits to each cell's annual values a generalised extreme value distribution by sample L-moments (the default for all four recipes), on H3 cells of resolution 5 by default, and writes the canonical hazard file.

statement.note: Not checked: these labels are written when the curve is fitted, which this draft does not run. `annual_extremes()` returns the four value columns only.
statement.text: Labels the fitted file with the store's address, the licence CC-BY-4.0, a Copernicus attribution with the retrieval year, the retrieval time, a checksum of the annual files' checksums, the window of years, `single_member` pooling and `annual_exceedance`.

sources.purpose: Best-track points of tropical cyclones by basin, as published, for inspection. Not asset winds or return-period curves.

statement.text: Requests `<root>/ibtracs.<subset>.list.v04r01.csv`, with the subset spelled exactly as one of the eleven names crc-sdk accepts.
Saves the response unchanged as `source.csv` and records its SHA-256. A download shorter than the announced length is refused.
Reads line 1 as column names and line 2 as units. Requires the columns SID, SEASON and ISO_TIME. The units go to the manifest only; they are not in the data.
Keeps every column, in the file's order, under NOAA's names.
Delivers every value as a string. Nothing is parsed into a number or a date, and no unit is converted.
Removes leading and trailing whitespace from every value.
Turns a value that is empty after trimming into null. NOAA marks a missing value with a single space.
Keeps every data row in the file's order. Rows are not dropped, merged, sorted or de-duplicated.
`for_storms(ids)` keeps the rows whose SID is in the list. These are track points, not complete storms across basin files.
`years(a, b)` keeps the rows whose SEASON, read as an integer, lies in a..b inclusive. SEASON is NOAA's season label, not the calendar year of the point.
Writes a manifest beside the snapshot with the address, version, subset, SHA-256, retrieval time, ETag, Last-Modified, units, a terms address and a citation. The batches themselves carry no metadata.

statement.note: Read in the code, not shown on data: showing it needs NOAA to change a file between two runs. Left to monitoring (phase V4).
statement.text: In `reuse` mode (the default) a cached snapshot is served without asking NOAA whether the file has changed. NOAA rewrites these files in place.

sources.notes: Draft. NOAA lists 126 stations with this product; ten are in Texas. A station without the product is answered with HTTP 200 and an empty body of the usual shape, which crc-sdk refuses. NOAA sends no ETag and no Last-Modified for these responses. The exceedance levels carry the datum label in capitals (MHHW) and the annual series in lower case (mhhw); crc-sdk passes both on as published. NOAA sometimes answers the same address with the values rounded to one decimal instead of two or three (seen 2026-11-12); crc-sdk delivers whichever answer it received.
sources.purpose: NOAA's published exceedance levels and annual extremes at tide stations, as published.

statement.text: Accepts a station only as a string of exactly seven digits 0-9; anything else raises ValueError before any request.

Makes three GET requests to `https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/dpapi/prod/webapi/product.json` with `name=extremewaterlevels`, the station and `units=metric`: one with nothing more (station), one with `details=exceedancelevels&levelType=high` (levels), one with `extremeType=annuals&levelType=high` (annuals). Low-water and monthly products are never requested.

statement.note: The check compares with a second download of the same address, so it also differs when NOAA answers the same address differently (step one-answer); it cannot tell the two apart.
statement.text: Saves each response unchanged as `source.json` and records its SHA-256 in a manifest beside it.
Asks each address once and takes that answer as the station's published values. Nothing asks a second time or compares two answers; the recorded SHA-256 is that of the one answer received.

statement.note: Read in the code, not shown on data: NOAA's responses are a few kilobytes and complete. No constructed test was written for it.
statement.text: Refuses a response longer than 4 MiB (4,194,304 bytes) or shorter than its announced Content-Length.

statement.note: On NOAA's data two of these rules fire: an empty station list (a station without the product) and a levels response without the station id (NOAA sent an error message in its place). Each of the other rules is confirmed on constructed responses only, in the tests.
statement.text: Refuses a station (ValueError, nothing cached) unless: the station response lists exactly one station with that id, a longitude in -180..180, a latitude in -90..90 and a non-empty epoch; the levels and annuals responses carry that id, `units` equal to `meters` and a non-empty datum; the two datum labels are equal when letter case is ignored; the annuals response has a non-empty notice, a trend that is null or a number, and for every extreme an integer year and a finite value; the levels response has a non-empty `GEV_HI.exceedanceLevels` in which every probability is in (0, 1] and not repeated, every return period is at least 1, every level is finite, and a confidence bound that is present lies on its side of the level. There is no rule about the length or completeness of the annual series.

`source_levels()` gives one row per entry of `GEV_HI.exceedanceLevels`, in NOAA's order, with eleven columns: the station id, then name, longitude, latitude and datum epoch from the station response repeated on every row, the datum label from the levels response, and NOAA's `probability`, `returnPeriod`, `level`, `lower90CI` and `upper90CI`. A missing confidence bound becomes null. The return period is NOAA's rounded label, not 1/probability. `GEV_LO` and the monthly groups are not delivered.

`annual_extremes()` gives one row per entry of `extremes` in the annuals response, in NOAA's order, with six columns: the station id, `year`, `value`, the datum label from the annuals response, the datum epoch from the station response and NOAA's notice repeated on every row. No year is added, dropped or filled.
Delivers numbers as 64-bit floats (the year as a 32-bit integer) with NOAA's values: nothing is rounded, no unit is converted (metres are requested and required) and no datum is transformed.

`source_info()` gives the whole station entry as NOAA sent it, the datum label and units of the levels response, and the trend, its units, its start and end dates and the notice of the annuals response. The trend (mm/yr) appears here only, not in the tables.

Writes for each response a manifest with the address, station id, resource name, SHA-256, retrieval time, ETag, Last-Modified, an attribution, a documentation address and a terms address. The tables themselves carry no metadata.
With `cache(dir, sha256={resource: digest})` a response whose SHA-256 is not the given one is refused with RuntimeError; the names accepted are station, levels and annuals.

statement.note: Read in the code and in crc-sdk's own test (tests/test_noaa_water_levels.py), not shown on data: showing it needs NOAA to fail or change between two requests.
statement.text: Keeps the three responses of one fetch together as one snapshot; `refresh` fetches all three again, moves a pointer to the new snapshot and deletes the old one, and a fetch that fails leaves the previous snapshot in place.

statement.note: Read in the code, not shown on data: showing it needs NOAA to change a response between two runs. Left to monitoring.
statement.text: In `reuse` mode (the default) a complete cached snapshot is served without asking NOAA whether the responses have changed. NOAA sends neither ETag nor Last-Modified for them.

sources.notes: Assessed on the stations the Texas data explorer uses: the first forty USW stations in the Texas box, 2000 to 2024. These are small airports whose records begin around 2005, so 592 of 1,000 station-years have a file, 8 stations reach 15 complete years and none reaches crc-sdk's default of 20. Days are UTC days: in Texas a UTC day runs from the local evening to the next. The values are extremes of sampled hourly temperature, not of an instrument's daily maximum and minimum.
sources.purpose: Annual extremes of hourly station temperature, fitted per station, as a local check on gridded curves.

statement.text: Reads one Parquet file per station and year, `<root>/<year>/parquet/GHCNh_<station>_<year>.parquet`. A file NOAA does not have (HTTP 404) gives a year with no value; other errors stop the run.
Reads eight columns by range requests tied to the file's ETag: STATION, DATE, LATITUDE, LONGITUDE, ELEVATION, temperature and its quality and source codes. Hourly files are not kept.
Reads DATE as a timestamp and keeps the reports of the requested station whose timestamp falls in the requested year. A report whose DATE cannot be read is dropped.

statement.note: In these files the excluded reports carried other quality codes. No report had code 1 or 5 from an unlisted source, so on NOAA's data the source lists were not put to the test; the offline tests exercise them on constructed files.
statement.text: Uses a temperature when its quality code is blank, or is 1 from one of fourteen listed source codes, or is 5 from one of eight listed source codes. Any other code excludes the report's value.
Uses a temperature only if it is a finite number between -93.2 and 61.8 degrees Celsius inclusive.
Takes the temperature in degrees Celsius as published. No unit is converted; the output is labelled degC.

Groups reports by UTC calendar day. For each day it counts all reports, the accepted reports and the distinct clock hours that hold an accepted report, and takes the lowest and highest accepted temperature.
Counts a day as valid when at least 18 distinct hours hold an accepted report (three quarters of 24, rounded up). Several reports in one hour count once.
Counts a year as complete when at least 90 per cent of its days are valid (329 of 365, 330 of 366).

For a complete year, takes the highest daily maximum (`temperature_max`) or the lowest daily minimum (`temperature_min`) over the valid days only. An incomplete year has no value. Values on days that are not valid are ignored.

statement.note: No station in these files moved or lacked coordinates, so the refusal was not seen on NOAA's data; the offline tests exercise it on constructed files.
statement.text: Places the station at the lowest latitude and lowest longitude reported in the year, with the lowest reported elevation (-999.9 read as missing). Refuses a station whose coordinates move by more than 0.05 degrees within a year.
Fits a curve for a station only when it has at least the policy's minimum of complete years (20 by default; 15 in the Texas data explorer). The minimum is applied per station.

statement.note: Confirmed here: the family named in the output. The fit itself (parameters, method, behaviour on short records) is not checked; it belongs to validation (phase V7).
statement.text: Fits a generalized extreme value distribution to annual maxima and a lower-tail Gumbel distribution to annual minima, both by L-moments.
Writes the licence (CC0-1.0), an attribution text, the latest retrieval time, a checksum over the cached daily files and the request into the curve file's metadata.

sources.purpose: River flood depth at published return periods, fitted to a curve per source pixel and placed on H3 cells.

statement.text: Reads the release from the publisher's README.txt (the text after 'Dataset version') and refuses to run when it is not the one written in the code (GloFAS 2.1.2, EFAS 3.1.1). The file addresses hold no version.
Offers the return periods written in the code: 10, 20, 50, 75, 100, 200 and 500 years for GloFAS, and also 30 and 40 for EFAS. The publisher's directory is not read.

For GloFAS, takes every tile of the publisher's tile index whose extent meets the box, tiles that only touch it included; one depth file per tile and return period. For EFAS, takes the one raster of Europe per return period, whatever the box.
With a cache, copies from each file the window of every pixel the box touches into a local GeoTIFF, values unchanged, and fits from those copies. A tile the box does not reach is left out.

statement.note: The contents of the manifest and its checksums are confirmed. That a later run does not ask the publisher again is read in the code; it was not run with the network off.
statement.text: Writes a manifest in the cache with the release, the time it was resolved, the box, the return periods, each file's address and the SHA-256 of each local copy. No checksum of the publisher's file is taken, and a later run that finds the manifest does not ask the publisher again.

statement.note: Run with a cache. Without one (stream mode) the code raises a different error, ValueError 'bounds do not intersect the raster'; that mode was not run.
statement.text: A box outside the raster gives no crop; when no file reaches the box the run ends with LookupError 'no JRC resources intersect area' (with a cache). The message does not name the dataset's extent.
A pixel equal to the file's nodata value (-9999), or not finite, has no depth at that return period. A pixel with no depth at any return period is skipped.
Fits a curve only to a pixel that has a depth at four or more return periods. Other pixels get no row and no message (the curated policy writes no diagnostics file).
Fits a Gumbel distribution by least squares to the pixel's depths at their return periods (probability 1 - 1/T). The curated policy sets no limit on the misfit.
A pixel whose depths are all equal, or decrease from one return period to the next, cannot be fitted and is skipped without a message (`on_fit_failure = "skip"`).

statement.note: Compared for a seeded sample of pixels in each area, not for every pixel.
statement.text: Gives each fitted pixel one row for every H3 cell its square overlaps, at the resolution asked for (`native` means 10). Rows of one cell are not combined: reducing them to one value per cell is left to the caller.

statement.note: Compared for a seeded sample of pixels in each area.
statement.text: Identifies a pixel by the SHA-256 of the dataset name, the tile and the pixel's row and column. With a cache the row and column are those of the local crop, not of the publisher's file.
Labels every row hazard `RiverineInundation`, pathway `historical`, horizon 0, curve type `gumbel_r`, and the file with the unit m, the release and the return-period range of the inputs.

Writes in the output file a uri naming the dataset, the box (to twelve significant digits), the tiles that gave a curve and the return periods. Licence, attribution, retrieval time and checksum are left empty.

statement.note: Confirmed in so far as crc-framework's values of the fitted curves equal the reference's at the published return periods and at 25 and 250 years, for a seeded sample of pixels. How far the curve lies from the published depths is reported as exploration, not as a check.
statement.text: Depths at any return period, the published ones included, are read from the fitted curve; the published depths are not kept.

sources.purpose: Annual extremes from bias-adjusted, downscaled daily model output at 0.25 degree, one model and member at a time.

statement.text: Reads one NetCDF file per variable, model, scenario, member and year from NASA's archive on AWS, by range requests. Nothing is cached and no checksum is taken.
Reads exactly the file version asked for (1.0 has no suffix in the file name; later ones end in `_v<version>`). A version NASA does not have fails; another is never substituted.
Accepts the file versions 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2.
Checks that the file's own attributes name the model, scenario, member and version that were asked for.

statement.note: The warning was seen on every file read. `strict_licence=True` was not run.
statement.text: Reads the model licence written in the file and keeps it beside NASA's archive licence (CC0-1.0). Warns when the file's licence is not CC0; refuses it when `strict_licence` is set.
Requires precipitation to be declared in kg m-2 s-1 and multiplies it by 86,400 to give millimetres per day.
Requires temperature to be declared in kelvin (K) and subtracts 273.15 to give degrees Celsius.

statement.note: The files read use the proleptic Gregorian calendar with 365 days and no gap. Other calendars and gaps were exercised only in the offline tests.
statement.text: Requires the daily time axis to be strictly increasing and to lie within the requested year, in the file's own calendar, and places each day by its date.

statement.note: Confirmed for a box of 44 by 53 cells. A box narrower than one cell and a box across the 180 degree meridian were not run.
statement.text: Selects the grid cells whose centres lie inside the box grown by half a cell on every side, with longitudes brought to -180..180 and ordered west to east. A box narrower than one cell is widened to two cells.
Treats the file's fill value as missing.

statement.note: In NASA's files a cell has either every day or none (ocean), so the 90 per cent line itself was crossed only in the offline tests.
statement.text: Gives a grid cell a value only when at least 90 per cent of the year's days are present.
`rx1day` is the largest daily value of the year. `rx5day` is the largest sum over five consecutive days that lie within the year; windows do not reach into the neighbouring years.

statement.note: Cannot be checked at crc-sdk 0.11.1, where both recipes fail (CRC-001-NEX). On a local clone that carries the fix, every cell agrees with the recomputation (checks `annual-fixed-clone`); that is not a statement about a released version.
statement.text: `txx` is the highest daily maximum of the year and `tnn` the lowest daily minimum.
Returns one row per grid cell that has a value, at the cell's centre, south to north and west to east. No distribution is fitted.

Labels every row with the unit, recipe, model, scenario, member, grid, version, calendar (under one name per calendar: `365_day` is written `noleap`), the file's address, the retrieval time, both licences and an attribution.
